title: Resumable uploads for large files
intent: Uploads over ~50 MB restart from zero whenever the network drops. Add server-side upload sessions backed by S3 multipart so a client can resume from the last confirmed byte.

questions.q: Where do partial uploads live while a session is open?
questions.consequence: This decides what the reaper in step 04 talks to, and whether abandoned bytes cost us storage. Changing it later means rewriting steps 01 and 04.
options: S3 multipart · native, no new storage
local disk staging · needs a volume + its own GC

questions.q: Should a resume work from a different device or browser?
questions.consequence: Cross-device resume means the session token has to be listable per user, which adds an endpoint and a permission check. Per-client keeps it to one opaque token.
questions.default: per-client token, 24h expiry, no listing endpoint

approach.thesis: Use the native S3 multipart upload id as the session primitive.
approach.rationale: One upload id per session, chunk N maps to part N, completion is a single CompleteMultipartUpload call. No second storage path to reason about and per-part checksums come for free.

dropped.why: Another migration, hand-rolled checksums, and it doubles write volume for every upload.
Right shape, but it needs its own auth adapter and a fresh dependency review.

steps.title: Upload session record + store
steps.rationale: Holds upload id, object key, chunk size, confirmed part list, owner and expiry. Everything else reads from this row, so it lands first.

steps.title: Session + chunk endpoints
steps.rationale: POST /uploads opens a session and returns the chunk size the client must use. PUT /uploads/:id/parts/:n is idempotent per part. HEAD /uploads/:id answers how far the client got.
steps.verify: 3-part upload, kill after part 2, resume, checksum match

steps.title: Client resume loop
steps.rationale: On any network error, HEAD the session, then continue from the first missing part with capped exponential backoff. The progress bar keeps its position instead of snapping to zero.

steps.title: Abandoned session reaper
steps.rationale: Hourly job aborts multipart uploads older than 24h and deletes their session rows. Written against whichever store Q1 lands on.
steps.verify: seed 3 stale sessions, run job, bucket lists 0 parts

steps.title: Remove legacy single-shot PUT path
steps.rationale: The old endpoint has no session semantics and would bypass the resume flow entirely once clients migrate.
steps.verify: grep -r legacyPut src/ returns nothing, e2e suite green

steps.title: Feature flag + rollout guard
steps.rationale: upload.resume gates the new flow so it can ship dark and revert without a deploy.
steps.verify: flag off serves old flow, flag on serves sessions

steps.title: Metrics for resumed and abandoned uploads
steps.rationale: Without these two counters we cannot tell whether the feature worked in production, which is half of the done-when list.
steps.verify: both counters visible in the staging dashboard

tests.expected: upload completes, one object, checksum matches
410 Gone, client restarts from byte 0 without an error toast
409, session untouched, no partial object written

tests.condition: 200 MB file on throttled 3G, airplane mode twice
tests.expected: resumes both times, progress never goes backwards

doneWhen: A 200 MB upload survives two network drops with no user action.
Success rate for files over 50 MB reaches 99% in staging over a week.
Bucket reports zero multipart uploads older than 24h.

risks.risk: Orphaned multipart parts keep billing after a user walks away.
risks.mitigation: reaper in step 04, plus a 7-day bucket lifecycle rule as a backstop

risks.risk: Client and server disagreeing on chunk size corrupts the assembled object.
risks.mitigation: server owns the number and echoes it in the session; client never guesses

callout: Biggest risk is money, not correctness: abandoned sessions leave paid-for parts in the bucket. The reaper plus a lifecycle rule covers it twice.
